setup: A flat one-chart emergent base with an explicitly constructed weak (fibrewise) solder datum whose frame jumps at one point.
intended_bad_shortcut: Declaring the fibrewise Task-34 solder sufficient for tangent geometry, so that no regularity condition is needed.
result: The local representative and the induced metric are both discontinuous; the weak datum is strictly weaker than a regular one.
scientific_role: Forces the regularity condition into the definition of the coupling primitive.
what_it_rules_out: Rules out reading the Task-34 fibrewise law as 'the emergent manifold carries a Lorentz metric'.

setup: The induced metric of the same weak solder.
intended_bad_shortcut: Assuming that a fibrewise-defined metric is automatically continuous or smooth.
result: The induced metric is not continuous on the chart domain.
scientific_role: Separates 'a bilinear form on each fibre' from 'a metric field'.
what_it_rules_out: Rules out claiming smooth Lorentzian geometry from the weak solder alone.

setup: The Moebius-type orientation-reversing periodic gluing, whose wrap-around tangent transition has determinant -1.
intended_bad_shortcut: Assuming that the bottom-up construction always produces a regular solder, i.e. that global topology never obstructs it.
result: No native Spin transition datum over this base admits a regular solder; the failure is located at the orientation gate.
scientific_role: Shows the regular solder is a genuine gate and that the orientation gate is sensitive.
what_it_rules_out: Rules out 'all four-manifolds admit the native solder' and any universal existence claim.

setup: An abstract two-patch cover with a kernel-valued sign twist of a native Spin datum.
intended_bad_shortcut: Assuming that the Spin-lift layer is vacuous, i.e. that the projection determines the lift.
result: Two native Spin data with the same projection are distinguished by the project's fixed-cover notion.
scientific_role: Shows the obstruction/lift layer has content.
what_it_rules_out: Rules out treating the native Spin datum as redundant information.

setup: The one-loop and two-loop periodic control bases with their two-component overlaps.
intended_bad_shortcut: Concluding that a bottom-up construction canonizes the Spin structure and removes the discrete lift freedom.
result: The freedom survives: two (resp. four) gauge-inequivalent lifts all admit regular solders.
scientific_role: Shows the reconvergence theorems do not secretly trivialise the lift choice.
what_it_rules_out: Rules out 'the construction selects a unique Spin structure'. It does NOT compute H^1(M; Z/2).

setup: An explicitly constructed co-varying scalar transport family, plus the general question of universal admissibility.
intended_bad_shortcut: Treating the closure observable as trivially satisfiable, which would make any positive smoke-test result vacuous.
result: There is no universal existence theorem, and the selective family is admissible exactly at the neutral value.
scientific_role: Anti-vacuity control for the Task-38 experiment.
what_it_rules_out: Rules out reading Task-38's universal admissibility as an artefact of a toothless predicate.

setup: The tested one-parameter Spin cocycle family on the frozen periodic control, compared at the project's kernel-valued equivalence.
intended_bad_shortcut: Using a degenerate equivalence relation under which everything is gauge equivalent.
result: At the kernel-valued relation a nonzero parameter value is NOT equivalent to the neutral one.
scientific_role: Shows that the positive gauge result uses a specific, non-degenerate relation and that the two relations are kept apart.
what_it_rules_out: Rules out the reading that 'any two cocycles are gauge equivalent anyway'.

setup: Abstract combinatorial Spin-foam-style labels on an adjacency structure.
intended_bad_shortcut: Claiming that combinatorial labelling data already produce the tangent coupling.
result: The labels are unconstrained and determine no solder.
scientific_role: Separates combinatorial data from differential-geometric coupling.
what_it_rules_out: Rules out a combinatorial shortcut to the solder. It says nothing about any published spin-foam model.

setup: The Moebius-type gluing carrying genuine native Spin transition data.
intended_bad_shortcut: Concluding from 'Spin-type data exist' that a tangent Lorentz coupling exists.
result: Native Spin data exist while no regular solder does.
scientific_role: Project-native separation of the internal Spin seed from tangent geometry.
what_it_rules_out: Rules out 'an internal Spin seed implies a Spin structure on the tangent bundle'. This is not the classical S^4 theorem.

setup: The one-chart base gluing with its trivial cover.
intended_bad_shortcut: Accepting gates that are closed for trivial reasons, i.e. that reject everything.
result: A regular solder exists, there is no overlap obstruction and no artificial sign family.
scientific_role: Positive control establishing the sensitivity of the negative ones.
what_it_rules_out: Rules out the possibility that the gates are vacuously restrictive.

setup: A continuous but non-differentiable self-homeomorphism of the local model used as a gluing map.
intended_bad_shortcut: Assuming that topological gluing automatically yields a smooth manifold.
result: The reconstructed space is charted but the smooth gate fails.
scientific_role: Shows that SmoothGluing is a genuine additional hypothesis.
what_it_rules_out: Rules out 'the emergent manifold is automatically smooth'.
